title: Design and Prototype Implementation of a Teleoperated Robot for Narrow-Well Rescue: ANGEL
content: Rescue of children trapped in narrow vertical wells requires remote intervention within a confined space while limiting further displacement of the victim. This paper presents the design and physical implementation of ANGEL (Advanced Narrow-well Guidance for Extraction and Lifesaving), a teleoperated robotic system for rescuing children trapped in narrow wells. The architecture integrates a suspended rescue capsule, a deployable mechanical retention device, two slave manipulators, corresponding master arms, an operator console, stereoscopic vision with three-dimensional visualization, and an environmental sensing subsystem using NUCLEO-WL55JC1 boards over a tethered RS-485 link for downhole monitoring. A central design principle is to position an expandable mechanical device below the victim before manipulation, providing a barrier against further sinking. The slave mechanisms combine a translational positioning stage, articulated rotary joints and a three-degree-of-freedom wrist. Corresponding master mechanisms provide direct motion references, while the stereoscopic interface supports observation of the intervention space. The system is described through an intended workflow comprising deployment, visual and sensor-based assessment, positioning, stabilization, teleoperated manipulation and preparation for extraction or continued support during conventional rescue operations. The contribution concerns the integrated design and its physical implementation.
